newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek yield curve stabilises in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek yield curve stabilises in late trade.

text.p: Greek money rates and forex forwards were hovering around morning levels in late dealings and bond traders said there was live trading on Thursday in FRNs due 2002 and 2003.
"Depos and forex forwards are little changed following a pick-up in rates in the morning," said a trader at a foreign bank. "There is plenty of cash around."
The central bank drained overnight money at an unchanged 12.40 percent.
Bond dealers reported active trading in FRNs due 2002 and 2003 unaffected by Monday's FRN auction.
"Monday's FRN auction should do well," said a trader at another foreign bank. "Local banks will bid aggressively for this FRN to replenish their bond holdings."
Greece will auction 250 billion drachmas of seven-year floaters with the first coupon set at 14 percent on Monday, October 21, the finance ministry said in a statement today.
The spread is held constant at 150 basis points but the benchmark 12-month T-bill is slashed by 20 basis points to 12.50 percent.

The treasury reserves the right to accept non-competitive bids up to 30 percent of the auctioned amount, it said. It also reserves the right not to accept all or some of the competitive bids to be submitted, the statement said.
It also reserves the right to accept competitive bids over the 250 billion drachma amount if non-competitive bids do not suffice to cover the 30 percent allotment.
The mark was quoted at 156.47/52 drachmas from Thursday's 156.490 fix, the dollar at 240.91/96 drachmas from 240.960 and the Ecu at 300.28/38 from 300.260 drachmas.
